messages.content: Find out about traffic laws in Texas.

function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
Here’s a concise overview of key Texas traffic laws and regulations: | Area | Key Points | Practical Tips | |------|------------|----------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits vary by road type (e.g., 55‑mph on rural interstates, 45‑mph on urban interstates).
• “No‑limit” highways (e.g., I‑10, I‑35) have no posted speed limit, but drivers must still drive at a safe speed for conditions. | • Always obey posted signs; if none, use common sense and adjust for weather, traffic, and road conditions. | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑Safety** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster.
• Texas has a “no‑seat‑belt” law for all ages. | • Check that every passenger is buckled before you start driving. | | **Cell‑phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use is illegal while driving.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed.
• Texting while driving is prohibited. | • Use a hands‑free system or pull over if you need to make a call. | | **Alcohol & Drugs** | • Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) limit is 0.08% for all drivers.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21 (BAC 0.02% or higher is a violation).
• DUI laws include mandatory ignition‑interlock devices for repeat offenders. | • Never drive after drinking; use rideshare, public transit, or a designated driver. | | **Traffic Signals & Signs** | • Red lights mean stop; green means go; yellow means prepare to stop.
• Stop signs require a full stop even if the intersection is clear.
• Right‑turn on red is allowed unless a sign prohibits it. | • Always come to a complete stop at stop signs and red lights, even if you’re the only vehicle. | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • Pedestrians always have right‑of‑way at crosswalks.
• School buses stopping for children have priority.
• Emergency vehicles with flashing lights have priority. | • Yield to pedestrians and stopped school buses; give way to emergency vehicles. | | **Lane Discipline** | • Keep to the right lane unless passing.
• Use turn signals at least 100 feet before changing lanes or turning. | • Signal early and keep to the right to avoid confusion. | | **Parking & Loading Zones** | • No parking within 20 feet of a fire hydrant.
• No parking in loading zones unless you’re loading/unloading.
• Parking on sidewalks is prohibited. | • Observe all parking signs; use designated loading zones only when loading. | | **School Bus Rules** | • Stop for a school bus with its stop sign extended and lights flashing, regardless of direction.
• Do not pass a stopped school bus until the sign is retracted. | • Treat school buses like any other stopped vehicle; stop and wait. | | **Vehicle Equipment** | • Headlights must be on from sunset to sunrise and during inclement weather.
• All vehicles must have working brakes, turn signals, and horn.
• Mirrors must be adjusted to provide adequate rear visibility. | • Check your mirrors and lights before each trip. | | **Insurance & Registration** | • Minimum liability insurance is required.
• Vehicle registration must be current and displayed on the rear license plate. | • Keep proof of insurance in the glove compartment; renew registration on time. | ### Quick Reference Checklist 1. **Seat belt** – All passengers buckled. 2. **Phone** – No handheld use; no texting. 3. **Speed** – Follow posted limits; adjust for conditions. 4. **Stop** – Full stop at stop signs and red lights. 5. **Yield** – Pedestrians, school buses, emergency vehicles. 6. **Signal** – 100‑ft advance for turns/lane changes. 7. **Parking** – No hydrant, sidewalk, or loading zone violations. 8. **Lights** – On from sunset to sunrise and during rain/snow. Feel free to ask if you’d like more detail on any specific area or if you’re looking for recent updates or case law!
